title: Psalm 133: How Good and Pleasant When Brothers Dwell Together
summary: The psalm celebrates the goodness of brothers living together in unity, and it compares that unity to fine oil poured on Aaron's head, running down his beard to his robes, and to the dew of Mount Hermon falling on the mountains of Zion. There, it says, the LORD has commanded his blessing: life forevermore.

line: The goodness of brothers living together in unity, like oil running down Aaron's beard and dew falling on Zion, where the LORD commands his blessing.
guide: Unity among God's people is a joy and not only a duty. Ask where there is a quarrel in your family or church that you could help to heal, and pray for unity as a gift that runs down from above.

stanzas.title: How good and pleasant is unity
Like oil on Aaron's head, running down
Like the dew of Hermon on Zion; the blessing of life

verses.t: A song of ascents. Of David. Behold, how good and pleasant it is when brothers live together in harmony!
It is like fine oil on the head, running down on the beard, running down Aaron’s beard over the collar of his robes.
It is like the dew of Hermon falling on the mountains of Zion. For there the LORD has bestowed the blessing of life forevermore.
